raw_response:
I farm only 2 mu by myself, and I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for 45 years in Quzhou County, so I will keep the system simple, steady, and low-risk. I will plant winter wheat on 2 mu first, then summer maize on the same 2 mu after wheat harvest. Because I am 65 and working alone, I will choose seed and field work that are reliable and not too labor-heavy. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, rotary tillage, and a few irrigations from my well because wheat here responds well to water at key stages. After harvest, I will quickly prepare the land and plant hybrid maize, because maize gives better yield with hybrid seed in our area. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level for maize too, use fewer irrigations than wheat, and do only the pesticide sprays I think are necessary. My goal is stable grain yield, manageable labor, and avoiding excessive cost on such a small farm.
